bear.writtenAnchor: The AI build-out that drove revenue from 60.9bn in FY2024 to 215.9bn in FY2026 proves to be a pull-forward: hyperscale customers digest the capacity they have bought, and NVIDIA's own filed history shows how fast this business can stall — revenue grew 0.2% in FY2023 and operating margin collapsed to 15.7% that year (H:revenue, H:margin). Growth flattens to low single digits off a very large base, pricing concessions and a heavier mix of lower-margin systems pull margin back toward the mid-30s, and the capital already deployed (invested capital rose from 45.4bn to 155.2bn in two years) earns far less than the 66-81% returns of the boom (H:returns). Stock compensation of 6.4bn a year keeps leaking share count (H:cashflow).

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: NVIDIA's own filed history contains a flat year: revenue grew 0.2% in FY2023 after the prior cycle peaked (H:revenue). The bear case repeats that digestion year as the steady rate off the much larger 215.9bn FY2026 base, inside the filed single-year range of 0.2% to 125.9%.

operatingMargin.text: Pricing pressure and a heavier systems mix pull margin back near the 33.0% long-run median and the 37.3% of FY2022, well above the 15.7% FY2023 trough but far below the 60.4% current level (H:margin). This is inside the permitted band of 5.7% to 67.4% around the filed 15.7%-62.4% range.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: With growth stalled the company spends little net new capital, reverting to the filed median net reinvestment of 1.1% of revenue (capex less depreciation), close to FY2024 when capex of 1,069m was below D&A of 1,508m (H:capex).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: If the cycle turns, new capital earns closer to the weak years of the filed record — ROIC was 11.2% in FY2023 and 15.6% in FY2021 (H:returns). A 14% return on new dollars is below the base and bull terminal returns and is permitted to sit near the discount rate in the bear case.

shareCount.text: Stock-based compensation has risen every year to 6,386m in FY2026; with no buyback figure in the supplied sources, the bear assumes grants are not offset and the diluted count creeps up about 4% over the forecast. (1.04× today's diluted count)

base.writtenAnchor: Demand stays strong but normalises off an enormous base. The July 2026 quarter was still running 105.9% ahead of the year-ago quarter with trailing revenue of 303.0bn, so the near-term run-rate is well above the FY2026 reported year (H:quarter, H:revenue); growth then decelerates sharply as the base compounds, settling at a high-teens constant rate for years 1-5. Operating margin holds in the mid-50s — below the 62.4% peak of FY2025 and the 60.4% of FY2026, reflecting mix shift into full systems and networking, but far above the 33.0% median of the longer history (H:margin). New capital keeps earning well: the last five years' incremental return on new capital was 75.2%, and the base case assumes roughly half of that persists before fading to the terminal return (H:returns). Net reinvestment stays light relative to revenue, as capex of 6.0bn against 2.8bn of depreciation on 215.9bn of revenue shows (H:capex).

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The latest quarter was 105.9% above the year-ago quarter and trailing revenue is 303.0bn against a FY2026 reported 215.9bn, so the entry run-rate is still accelerating (H:quarter, H:revenue); growth then decelerates hard on a base this size, and 18% a year for years 1-5 sits well inside the filed 0.2%-125.9% single-year range.

operatingMargin.text: Margin settles between the FY2024 level of 54.1% and the FY2026 level of 60.4%, giving back some of the peak 62.4% to mix and cost of full-system shipments while staying far above the 33.0% median (H:margin).

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: FY2026 capex of 6,042m less D&A of 2,843m is about 1.5% of 215,938m of revenue, up from the 1.1% median, as capacity and supply commitments scale (H:capex, H:revenue); the base lifts this modestly to 2.0% for the growth assumed.

returnOnNewInvestment.text: The incremental return on new capital over the last five years was 75.2% and FY2026 ROIC was 66.4%; the base assumes roughly half of that incremental return persists on new dollars before fading to the 14.0% terminal return (H:returns). It is well under the 1.5x cap on the 81.2% best filed return.

shareCount.text: Annual stock-based compensation of 6,386m keeps issuing shares, but operating cash flow of 102,718m in FY2026 funds repurchases that absorb most of it, leaving a small net increase (H:cashflow). (1.02× today's diluted count)

bull.writtenAnchor: Accelerated computing keeps absorbing a growing share of global data-centre spend and NVIDIA holds its position across silicon, networking and software. Revenue compounds near 30% a year off a base that already grew 105.9% year-on-year in the latest quarter (H:quarter), operating margin returns toward the FY2025 peak of 62.4% as scale and software mix offset system costs (H:margin), and incremental capital keeps earning close to the 75.2% incremental return of the last five years and the 81.2% peak ROIC (H:returns). Operating cash flow of 102.7bn funds growth internally and lets repurchases absorb the 6.4bn annual stock-compensation charge, holding share count flat (H:cashflow).

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: Sustained demand keeps the compound rate near 30%, far below the 46.6% nine-year window CAGR and the 125.9% best filed year, and supported by the 105.9% year-on-year growth in the quarter ended 2026-07-26 (H:revenue, H:quarter).

operatingMargin.text: Margin returns to the filed peak of 62.4% achieved in FY2025 and just above the 60.4% of FY2026, which is within the filed range and below the 67.4% ceiling allowed (H:margin).

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Faster growth needs more net capital than the 1.5% of revenue implied by FY2026 capex of 6,042m against D&A of 2,843m on 215,938m of revenue, so net reinvestment runs at 3.0% of revenue (H:capex, H:revenue).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: New capital keeps earning near the FY2026 realised ROIC of 66.4% and below the 75.2% five-year incremental return and the 81.2% peak, so it stays inside the 1.5x cap and above the 15.5% bull terminal return (H:returns).

shareCount.text: Operating cash flow of 102,718m in FY2026 is more than fifteen times the 6,386m stock-compensation charge, so buybacks fully offset issuance and share count is flat (H:cashflow). (1× today's diluted count)

moatAnchor.text: Intangible assets — the accelerated-computing platform and its software stack — reinforced by customer switching costs once workloads are written for it. The filed returns support the credit: ROIC was 57.4% in FY2024, 81.2% in FY2025 and 66.4% in FY2026, with an incremental return on new capital of 75.2% over the last five years, all far above the 11.0% discount rate and above the 14.0% terminal return the wide credit implies (H:returns). Revenue rising from 26,974m in FY2023 to 215,938m in FY2026 while operating margin went from 15.7% to 60.4% shows pricing power rather than volume-only expansion (H:revenue, H:margin).

constantsAnchor.text: No company tax disclosure was supplied, so NOPAT uses the general US federal statutory rate of 21.0% (STATUTORY), which is also the rate used to build the filed NOPAT and ROIC series (H:returns). The stress margin of 25% is below both the current 60.4% and the 33.0% median, and sits between the FY2023 trough of 15.7% and the FY2020 level of 26.1% (H:margin).

provenance.measurementConvention: Yearly reset measured as Damodaran's published implied expected return on the S&P 500 (8.99% in his October 2026 update), rounded to the nearest 0.5% — an AI DEFAULT inside the D1 rule, reconciled 17 Oct 2026; the annual methodology review may change it. Provenance, not a rule value.

provisionalLabels.preRevenueConstructionLeadYears: First-order estimate; worth $27/share on OKLO's 8 GW case (§7.1).
provisionalLabels.leveredCostOfEquityCap: No observations behind the 30% level itself; capped cells are labelled RATE CAPPED — VALUE IS AN UPPER BOUND (I12, §7.1).
provisionalLabels.gate0InterestIncomeOverRevenueThreshold: No observations behind it (Appendix B); the other three Gate 0 tests are classification lookups, not thresholds (§6.1).
provisionalLabels.gate1HistoryInsufficientYears: Red-team judgment with no observations (Appendix B). Direction of error is suppression, so a wrong threshold shows less rather than something false (§6.2).
provisionalLabels.gate1ShortHistoryYears: Red-team judgment with no observations (Appendix B), same basis as the <5-year threshold (§6.2).
provisionalLabels.historyInsufficientStressMarginRelativeR: No observations; substitutes for a median that does not exist under HISTORY INSUFFICIENT (§6.2).
provisionalLabels.runRateSequentialGrowthTrigger: Calibrated on NVIDIA only (Appendix B) (§7.2 M12).
provisionalLabels.seasonalityPriorYearThreshold: Comes from I4 and has no observations behind it (§7.2 M12).
